question: Why do the authors say many earlier spreadsheet benchmarks are a poor match for professional finance work?
options: They use only small language models that cannot handle formulas
They give detailed instructions for simple, checkable operations, whereas real finance requests are underspecified and multi-step
They ignore formatting entirely, which never matters in finance
They test only question answering over live market data

private.explanation: The paper says prior work focuses on formula generation, atomic edits, flat tables or fixed-sheet QA that map cleanly to programmatic checks. Real requests are naturally phrased and expect the agent to infer a plan. Formatting does matter in finance, which is why BLUEFIN includes Presentation criteria.
